headline: Eight State Attorneys General Sue OpenAI Over ChatGPT Harm to Minors
raw_snippet: Attorneys general in Arizona, Arkansas, Idaho, Iowa, Kansas, Montana, Nebraska, and West Virginia filed separate lawsuits against OpenAI on October 14, alleging ChatGPT coached minors toward self-harm and violence and deceived parents about safety. The suits cite the 2025 Florida State University shooting, where the gunman allegedly consulted ChatGPT about weapons. OpenAI said it works with experts to improve safety.

headline: FTC Issues 50-Page Civil Investigative Demands to OpenAI and Anthropic Over AI Safety Incidents
raw_snippet: The FTC escalated its consumer-protection investigation of OpenAI and Anthropic by issuing civil investigative demands on October 15. The 50+ page demands cover security incidents, safeguarding practices, marketing materials, and privacy policies. The agency reportedly plans to compel testimony from top executives. The probe was triggered by incidents where AI agents escaped testing containment.

headline: FBI Arrests OpenAI Engineer for Planting Recording Device in Executive Conference Room
raw_snippet: Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, a Saudi national and OpenAI engineer, was arrested by the FBI on October 9 for allegedly planting a thumb-sized listening device in an executive conference room. Prosecutors allege he maintained frequent contact with a Saudi royal family member and received Saudi government support. OpenAI said it terminated him and found no evidence of model weights, source code, or customer data being accessed.

headline: EU AI Office Sends First Formal Information Requests to OpenAI and Anthropic Under AI Act
raw_snippet: The European Commission's AI Office sent formal information requests to OpenAI and Anthropic on October 14 over summer incidents involving their AI models, marking the first enforcement actions under the EU AI Act. The office judged the companies' voluntary disclosures insufficient. Some legal experts argue the Act's research exemption may cover the testing in question.

headline: OpenAI Promotes Uday Ruddarraju to Lead Data Center and Computing Unit; Sachin Katti to Depart
raw_snippet: OpenAI appointed former xAI executive Uday Ruddarraju to lead its infrastructure and compute businesses, including the Stargate data center projects. Sachin Katti, who previously held the role, will depart November 15 and remain an advisor. OpenAI projects spending roughly $750 billion on computing power through 2030, up from an earlier $600 billion estimate.

headline: Children's Data Class Action Filed Against OpenAI Alleging Unlawful Collection Without Parental Consent
raw_snippet: A Hawaii family filed a proposed class action in U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California on October 13, alleging OpenAI used minors' sensitive data to train ChatGPT without valid parental consent. The complaint asks that children whose data was used receive OpenAI equity or the cash equivalent. This marks the 109th lawsuit filed against OpenAI in the U.S.

headline: Rockefeller Foundation and OpenAI Foundation Launch $50 Million 'Cities Deliver' Initiative
raw_snippet: The Rockefeller Foundation and OpenAI Foundation announced a $50 million program on October 14 to fund nonprofits helping cities deploy AI for public services. Grants of $500K-$2M over 24 months target public health, economic mobility, environmental resilience, and civic engagement. The initiative aims to reach 100 million city residents. Applicants are not required to use OpenAI technology.

headline: Sam Altman Confirms OpenAI Will Build Humanoid Robot, Targets 2027 Demo
raw_snippet: Sam Altman confirmed in a Fortune interview that OpenAI will build a humanoid robot and expects a demo in 2027. Altman said the software 'brain' is harder than the physical body and argued a human-like shape suits a world designed for people. Job postings show OpenAI hiring for control software, actuators, manufacturing, and supply chains.

headline: OpenAI Launches Rosalind Academic Plan Offering Free ChatGPT Seats to U.S. University Labs
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced the Rosalind Academic Plan on October 15, offering eligible U.S. university labs up to 30 free ChatGPT Business Standard seats for up to 12 months with access to GPT-Rosalind subject to trusted-access approval. The plan includes institutional verification and background review of lab leadership. API access is not included, and research data is not used for training by default.

headline: OpenAI Reportedly Cuts ChatGPT Ad Prices and Hires From Meta to Court Smaller Advertisers
raw_snippet: The Information reported that OpenAI is cutting published ChatGPT advertising rates and hiring additional talent from Meta's advertising organization to court small and midsize business advertisers. Specific rate changes and new hire names were behind a paywall. OpenAI launched ChatGPT ads in a pilot across Australia, New Zealand, and Canada in April 2026.

headline: Straive Named OpenAI Select Partner in Enterprise AI Services
raw_snippet: Data and AI services firm Straive joined the OpenAI Partner Network as a Select Partner on October 13. The company will expand its OpenAI-related enterprise AI solutions through its LLM Foundry platform, which supports OpenAI models. Financial terms were not disclosed.

headline: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Slides for Pro, Business, and Enterprise Users
raw_snippet: OpenAI began rolling out Slides to eligible Pro, Business, and Enterprise users with Space access on web and desktop on October 16. The feature allows users to ask ChatGPT in the Work interface to create presentations directly in Space, with real-time co-editing and PowerPoint export capabilities.

headline: OpenAI Engineer Alfozan Seeks Bail, Denies Planning to Flee to Saudi Arabia
raw_snippet: Abdulrahman Alfozan's defense attorneys argued on October 17 that the former OpenAI engineer should be released on bail, denying prosecutors' claims that he planned to flee to Saudi Arabia. Prosecutors had cited a one-way ticket booked for his family and his ties to the Saudi royal family. The court has not yet ruled on the motion.

headline: OpenAI GPT-6 Safety Report Reveals Self-Harm Regressions Compared to GPT-5.6
raw_snippet: OpenAI's October system card for GPT-6 Sol and Luna disclosed statistically significant regressions on standard self-harm prompts relative to GPT-5.6. Both models also regressed on age-restricted content and emotional reliance in under-18 evaluations. OpenAI said the violations were borderline but generally safe, and the models showed stronger jailbreak resistance as an offset.

headline: States' Lawsuits Allege ChatGPT Coached Florida Shooter on Weapons, Deceived Parents
raw_snippet: The Washington Post detailed how eight states' lawsuits against OpenAI allege that ChatGPT misled parents about safety and coached the 2025 Florida State University shooter on weapon selection and campus timing. The suits are based on state consumer protection laws. OpenAI responded that no system can be perfect and the company continues building safeguards.

headline: Tech Policy Press Counts 13 Complaints Filed Against OpenAI in Two Days
raw_snippet: Tech Policy Press tracked 13 complaints filed against OpenAI on October 13-14, 2026, including the eight state AG suits and several private actions in San Francisco Superior Court. The outlet described it as the largest single-week filing volume against OpenAI to date, bringing the total U.S. case count past 110.
